root.meaning: of the same parents; full brother
root.note: From germen ‘sprout, bud’. In Latin, frāter germānus was a full brother, as opposed to a half-brother.

history: The Latin word for brother was frāter. But Romans could be more exact: a frāter germānus was a full brother, with the same father and mother, from germen, ‘sprout’, the same seed. In the west of the Empire people dropped frāter and kept the adjective, so germānus became the brother himself. Portuguese wore it down to irmão, Spanish to hermano. French and Italian stayed with frāter: frère and fratello. Frāter is not lost in Portuguese either. It lives in frade and frei, ‘friar, brother in a religious order’, and in fraterno, ‘brotherly’. Your sister is a irmã, and brothers and sisters together are os irmãos.
historyEinfach: Irmão means ‘brother’. A sister is a irmã. The word comes from Latin germānus, which meant ‘with the same parents’. Spanish hermano comes from the same word. French frère and Italian fratello come from another Latin word, frāter.

elsewhere.text: Catalan kept the same Latin word and more of its shape.
French and Italian kept the old Latin brother, frāter.
